data.title: Luliconazole 1% cream
data.summary: I Antifungals — Azoles · Imidazole (ketene dithioacetal structure) — newest topical azole
data.body:
_Topicals · I Antifungals — Azoles_

**Class:** Imidazole (ketene dithioacetal structure) — newest topical azole

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits 14-α-demethylase; very low MICs against dermatophytes (among the most potent topical azoles)
- High stratum corneum retention → short, once-daily courses

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Tinea corporis, cruris and pedis (approved)
- Cutaneous candidiasis, pityriasis versicolor
- Onychomycosis (10% solution in Japan)

## Dose & formulations
- Once daily: tinea corporis/cruris for 1 week, interdigital tinea pedis for 2 weeks (FDA label)
- In Indian practice with chronic/recurrent tinea, courses of 2–4 weeks are common

## Adverse effects
- Application-site irritation, contact dermatitis (rare)

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; animal data reassuring; use if needed.

## Viva points
- Most potent topical azole against dermatophytes
- Once daily, short course
- Widely used in India — rising resistance concerns with misuse

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.42 (luliconazole); Khopkar edition predates it. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
